subject: Immediate Exec Brief: Prospecta production throughput collapse behind transit proxy
participants_external: julia.chen@prospecta.com (Julia Chen, Head of Platform, Prospecta)
messages:
From: Julia Chen <julia.chen@prospecta.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 15:26:00 -0500
Subject: Urgent: production latency spike & 502 surge (Prospecta storefront)

Marcus / Marissa —

We started seeing a dramatic (3-4x) increase in API latency for the Prospecta storefront at ~14:40 UTC and a corresponding increase in 5xx errors (mainly 502/504). This is impacting checkout flows for ~18% of traffic and causing visible revenue impact. Attached are a pcap for a few failed requests and our Grafana snapshots (prospecta-net-trace.tar.gz).

Key details:
- First observed: 2026-11-02T14:39:02Z
- Scope: prod region-us-west; traffic routed via Redwood edge proxy cluster e-cluster-12
- Symptom: high connect time, TCP retransmits, backend 502/504 returned from edge proxy

We need an urgent bridge with SRE and Redwood execs. We are preparing a short impact summary for our leadership and would like an ETA on mitigation and root cause. Our renewal review is next week and this is timing-critical.

Can you confirm receipt and propose immediate next steps?

Thanks,
Julia Chen
Head of Platform, Prospecta
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Julia Chen <julia.chen@prospecta.com>, ops@prospecta.com
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 15:33:00 -0500
Subject: Fwd: Urgent: production latency spike & 502 surge (Prospecta storefront)

Team — forwarding Prospecta alert. They report a significant latency/5xx spike affecting checkout. Julia attached network traces; customer is asking for an exec bridge and an ETA on mitigation.

Immediate asks:
- Stephanie / SRE: can you confirm whether this looks like a pure networking egress issue (peering/DNS/firewall/proxy) or if the runtime is implicated?
- Vivek / Infra Eng: can you pull inference runtime metrics (KV cache hit rate, fanout, tail-latency per instance) for the same time window?
- Rafael / Edge: verify recent proxy config changes and if any autoscaling anomalies occurred on e-cluster-12.

Proposed next step: 30m bridge now if you can. If not, reply with earliest possible mitigation (route pin, firewall session cleanup, proxy rollback). I will prepare an executive summary and coordinate with Prospecta.

Marcus Lin
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: production latency spike & 502 surge (Prospecta storefront)

Adding initial SRE findings (quick triage):
- Observed spike aligns with a BGP path change reported by our cloud provider at 14:37 UTC that shifted egress traffic for a subset of subnets to a different transit AS.
- The alternate path shows elevated RTT and packet loss toward Prospecta's ISP; tcpdump from the edge shows multiple SYN retransmits and connection resets between 14:38–14:52 UTC.
- Edge proxy logs: connection pool exhaustion errors and an increase in 502s due to upstream connect failures (connection timeout).

Immediate mitigations in-flight:
1) We initiated firewall session table flush on affected edge nodes (started 14:55 UTC).
2) Pinning routing at the edge to the previous preferred peer for Prospecta prefixes (rollback announced to peering controller at 15:01 UTC).
3) Temporarily increasing connection pool size on e-cluster-12 (15:05 UTC) to avoid immediate 502s while routing stabilizes.

I attached the trimmed tcpdump and a short config diff (edge-proxy-config-diff.txt). Will follow up with more telemetry within 30–60 minutes.

—Stephanie
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 17:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Fwd: Urgent: production latency spike & 502 surge (Prospecta storefront)

Thanks for the triage notes, Stephanie. I pulled inference runtime metrics for Prospecta's production shards covering 14:30–15:30 UTC:
- KV cache miss rate increased from baseline 7% -> 42% during the incident window (cache warm/rebuild behavior suggests many sessions were rehydrating due to long tail reconnects).
- Request fanout per customer request increased by ~18% (retries and additional middleware hops).
- Model host CPU and GPU utilization unchanged; model latency internal is stable, indicating issue is path/connectivity not model execution.

My recommendation:
- Approve edge-level route pinning and connection pool bump (these are already deployed by SRE).
- Roll back the latest proxy config change that introduced an L7 connection pooling change last week (rollback is safe and will revert to previous pooling behavior). I propose a progressive canary: reroute 30% of Prospecta traffic to the older proxy version in us-west and monitor for 20 minutes.

If approved I will coordinate the canary (will need 10m to prepare and 30m monitor window). If the canary shows reduction in 502s and latency, increase to 60% and then complete cutover.

—Vivek
Engineering Manager, Runtime & Edge
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: CEO Leadership <ceo@redwood.com>, Ops Leadership <ops_leads@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Julia Chen <julia.chen@prospecta.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Exec summary & approval request — Prospecta production impact (US-West)

TL;DR — Prospecta is experiencing a production throughput collapse (~18% of checkout traffic affected) caused by an asymmetric network egress path (provider BGP change) that stressed our edge proxy connection pools and produced a spike in 502/504 responses. SRE has applied immediate mitigations (session table flush, routing pin, connection pool bump). Engineering recommends a canary rollback of last week's proxy pooling change for 30% of traffic.

Impact:
- Customer: Prospecta (strategic renewal next week)
- Scope: Production us-west; ~18% of requests saw elevated latency/5xx between 14:39–15:15 UTC on 2026-11-02
- Business risk: Checkout failures impacting revenue; customer has flagged renewal review

Proposed actions (need exec sign-off):
1) Approve canary rollback to previous proxy version for 30% of Prospecta us-west traffic (estimated 10m prep + 30m monitor).
2) Approve customer remediation gesture: 2 weeks service credit and an incident RCA within 72 hours.
3) Ask Partnerships to engage with cloud transit provider for a post-incident peering review and SLA remediation (Rafael to coordinate).

Expected timeline: canary start on approval, preliminary results in ~40 minutes, full cutover within 3 hours if successful.

Requesting approval from: CEO Leadership / Ops Leadership.

Marcus Lin
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Julia Chen <julia.chen@prospecta.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exec summary & approval request — Prospecta production impact (US-West)

Marcus —

Thanks for the fast response and the clear mitigation plan. We authorize the canary rollback and appreciate the proposed service credit. Please keep us updated every 4 hours until the RCA is published.

A couple of requests from our side:
- Please include the full tcpdump slices and BGP updates in the RCA (we need these for our post-mortem).
- Confirm that there will be no config changes during our renewal discussion this week without explicit notification.

We will provide a short impact summary for our execs and will hold off the renewal finalization until we receive the RCA.

Julia Chen
Head of Platform, Prospecta
